stem: Asha marks every point on her page that is exactly 4 cm away from a point P. What shape do all these points form?
options: A straight line of length 4 cm through P
A circle with centre P and radius 4 cm
A square with P as a corner and side 4 cm
A circle with centre P and radius 2 cm
explanation: Correct option: (B). All points at the same distance from a fixed point make a circle; the fixed point P is its centre and the common distance, 4 cm, is its radius. A line or a square has points at many different distances from P, and a radius of 2 cm would put the points only 2 cm away from P.

stem: To draw a circle of radius 4 cm, a compass is opened against a ruler. Which distance must be set to 4 cm?
options: The distance between the needle tip and the pencil tip
The full length of the compass arm that holds the pencil
The distance between the hinge and the pencil tip
The distance between the hinge and the needle tip
explanation: Correct option: (A). The needle stays fixed at the centre and the pencil traces the circle, so the radius is the gap between the needle tip and the pencil tip. The arm lengths and the distances from the hinge do not equal the radius of the circle drawn.

stem: In the 'Wavy Wave', the central line AB is 8 cm long and is covered by two identical half circles, the first from A to X. What radius should be set in the compass?
options: 8 cm
4 cm
2 cm
1 cm
explanation: Correct option: (C). Two identical half circles share the 8 cm line, so AX = 8 / 2 = 4 cm. AX is the diameter of the first half circle, so its radius is 4 / 2 = 2 cm. 4 cm is the diameter, not the radius; 8 cm is the whole line; 1 cm would need four half circles of diameter 2 cm.

stem: A circle has centre P and radius 3 cm. Point Q is 3 cm from P, point R is 2 cm from P and point S is 4 cm from P. Which of these points lie on the circle?
options: R only
Q and R
Q and S
Q only
explanation: Correct option: (D). Only points exactly one radius (3 cm) from the centre lie on the circle, so Q is on it. R at 2 cm lies inside the circle and S at 4 cm lies outside it, so any choice including R or S is wrong.

stem: Lata draws a wave of identical half circles, each of radius 1.5 cm, side by side along a central line 12 cm long, with no gaps. How many half circles fit exactly on the line?
explanation: Correct option: (C). Each half circle covers its diameter on the line: 2 x 1.5 cm = 3 cm. So the number of half circles is 12 / 3 = 4. The answer 8 comes from dividing by the radius instead of the diameter; 6 and 3 do not fill 12 cm exactly with 3 cm pieces.

stem: According to the chapter, which two properties does every rectangle satisfy?
options: All four sides are equal and all angles are 90°
Opposite sides are equal and all angles are 90°
Adjacent sides are equal and opposite angles are equal
All four sides are equal and all angles are 60°
explanation: Correct option: (B). A rectangle satisfies R1 (opposite sides are equal) and R2 (all angles are 90°). All four sides equal is the extra property of a square, which not every rectangle has; adjacent sides need not be equal, and a 4-sided figure with four 60° angles cannot exist.

DCBA
ABDC
CDAB

stem: A square sheet of paper is turned so that it stands on one of its corners. What can you say about the turned sheet?
options: It is no longer a square, since its sides now look slanted
It is a square only when one side is kept horizontal
Its sides stay equal but its angles are no longer 90°
It is still a square; its sides and angles are unchanged
explanation: Correct option: (D). Rotating a figure does not change its lengths or its angles. The turned sheet still has all sides equal and all angles 90°, so it satisfies both properties of a square. Slanting sides or the position on the page do not matter, and the angles stay 90°.

stem: Which statement about squares and rectangles is correct?
options: Every square is also a rectangle
Every rectangle is also a square
No square can be called a rectangle
A square is a rectangle only when rotated
explanation: Correct option: (A). A square has all sides equal, so its opposite sides are equal, and all its angles are 90°. It therefore satisfies both rectangle properties R1 and R2. A rectangle such as 4 cm by 6 cm is not a square, and rotating a figure does not change what it is.

stem: On a dot grid, Ravi starts at P and goes 2 dots right and 1 dot up to Q, then 1 dot left and 2 dots up to R, then 2 dots left and 1 dot down to S, then 1 dot right and 2 dots down back to P. What is PQRS?
options: A rotated square
A rotated rectangle that is not a square
A 4-sided figure with no right angles
A square only if the grid is turned
explanation: Correct option: (A). Every side spans 2 dots one way and 1 dot the other way, so all four sides are equal. At each corner the moves swap (2 across and 1 up becomes 1 across and 2 up), which makes the sides meet at right angles. So PQRS has equal sides and 90° angles: a square, just rotated. It is not merely a rectangle with unequal sides, it does have right angles, and turning the grid does not change the figure.

stem: To construct a square PQRS of side 6 cm, PQ = 6 cm is drawn first. What is the next step?

Mark the midpoint of PQ with a ruler

10 cm

stem: While constructing square PQRS with PQ = 6 cm, S is marked on the perpendicular at P. Why must PS be 6 cm?
options: All sides of a square are equal, so PS = PQ
PS is opposite to PQ, and opposite sides are equal
The 90° angle at P fixes PS at exactly 6 cm
The diagonal of the square must be 6 cm long
explanation: Correct option: (A). PS and PQ are adjacent sides meeting at P, and in a square all sides are equal, so PS = PQ = 6 cm. PS is not opposite to PQ (RS is). The right angle fixes the direction of PS, not its length, and the diagonal of a 6 cm square is longer than 6 cm.

stem: Is it possible to construct a 4-sided figure in which all the angles are 90° but the opposite sides are not equal?
options: Yes, by making just one of its sides a little longer
Yes, but only if no side of it is horizontal
No, four right angles make the opposite sides equal
No, because such a figure is always a square
explanation: Correct option: (C). If all four angles are 90°, the figure is a rectangle and its opposite sides turn out equal, so such a figure cannot be drawn. Lengthening one side breaks the right angles, turning the figure does not change it, and the figure need not be a square since adjacent sides may differ.

stem: Ravi draws PQ = 10 cm and perpendiculars at P and Q. He marks S with PS = 2 cm but, by mistake, marks R with QR = 3 cm, and joins SR. Which statement about PQRS is correct?
options: Angles at R and S are not 90°, and PS is not equal to QR
It is a rectangle, because angles P and Q are 90°
All its angles are 90°, but SR is shorter than PQ
Only the angle at R fails to be 90°; the angle at S stays 90°
explanation: Correct option: (A). Since PS = 2 cm and QR = 3 cm, the line SR slopes, so it cannot meet the perpendiculars at right angles; both angles R and S are not 90°, and R1 fails as PS is not equal to QR. Two right angles at P and Q are not enough for a rectangle, and the angle at S changes along with the angle at R.

12 cm
9 cm
3 cm

stem: In rectangle ABCD, X moves along side AD and Y moves along side BC. Which length does the farthest distance between X and Y equal?
options: The side AB of the rectangle
The side BC of the rectangle
The sum of the sides AB and BC
The diagonal AC or BD
explanation: Correct option: (D). XY is longest when X and Y are at opposite corners, such as X = A and Y = C, or X = D and Y = B; then XY is a diagonal. AB is the shortest distance (when X and Y are level), BC is shorter than a diagonal, and the straight distance can never be as long as AB + BC.

stem: Which rectangle can NOT be divided into two identical squares?
options: 4 cm by 2.5 cm
8 cm by 4 cm
6 cm by 3 cm
5 cm by 2.5 cm
explanation: Correct option: (A). A rectangle splits into two identical squares only when its longer side is twice its shorter side. 8 = 2 x 4, 6 = 2 x 3 and 5 = 2 x 2.5, but 2 x 2.5 = 5, not 4, so the 4 cm by 2.5 cm rectangle cannot be divided this way.

stem: A square of side 4 cm is drawn inside a rectangle of sides 8 cm and 4 cm so that both have the same centre. How far is each side of the square from the nearer 4 cm side of the rectangle?
options: 4 cm
1 cm
3 cm
2 cm
explanation: Correct option: (D). The square fills the full 4 cm height, leaving 8 - 4 = 4 cm of the length. Since the centres match, this is shared equally on both sides: 4 / 2 = 2 cm. 4 cm forgets to share the gap, while 1 cm and 3 cm would put the square off-centre or give the wrong gap.

A rectangle whose length is twice its width
Any rectangle, whatever its side lengths
No rectangle, whatever its side lengths

stem: To construct a rectangle with DC = 5 cm and diagonal DB = 7 cm, a perpendicular line l is drawn to DC at C. How can B be located on l without trial and error?
options: Draw an arc of radius 5 cm centred at C to cut l
Draw an arc of radius 7 cm centred at C to cut l
Measure 5 cm along l from C with a ruler
Draw an arc of radius 7 cm centred at D to cut l
explanation: Correct option: (D). B lies on l and is 7 cm from D, because DB is the diagonal. All points 7 cm from D lie on a circle centred at D, so the arc of radius 7 cm from D meets l at B. Arcs centred at C give points at that distance from C, not from D, and CB is not given as 5 cm.

stem: Meena tries to construct a rectangle with one side DC = 7 cm and a diagonal of 5 cm, using the arc method from D. What happens?
options: It works: the 5 cm arc from D meets line l at point B
It fails, as the 5 cm arc from D never meets line l
It works, but only if the other side is 2 cm
It fails, as the diagonal is not twice the side
explanation: Correct option: (B). Every point on the perpendicular l at C is at least 7 cm from D (C itself is the nearest), so a 5 cm arc from D cannot reach l. stem: In the House construction, BC = 5 cm. How is point A, which is 5 cm from both B and C, located without trial and error?
options: Draw a circle of radius 5 cm centred at the midpoint of BC
Measure 5 cm straight up from B with a ruler and mark it
Draw 5 cm arcs from B and from C; their meeting point is A
Draw one arc of radius 5 cm from B and pick any point on it
explanation: Correct option: (C). Points on the arc from B are 5 cm from B and points on the arc from C are 5 cm from C, so their meeting point is 5 cm from both: that is A. A circle centred at the midpoint, a point straight above B, or any point on just one arc need not be 5 cm from both B and C.

stem: Two circles of radius 5 cm are drawn, centred at B and at C. How far is a point where they intersect from B and from C?
options: 5 cm from B and 10 cm from C
5 cm from both B and C
10 cm from both B and C
2.5 cm from both B and C

stem: In the House, after A is located, the curved roof is drawn with the compass tip at A and radius 5 cm. Why does this arc pass through both B and C?

Because B and C are 10 cm apart
Because A is the midpoint of BC
Because AB and AC are both 5 cm

stem: In the House, BC = 5 cm and A is found 5 cm from both B and C. Which statement about the triangle ABC is correct?

AB and AC are 5 cm, but BC is 10 cm
Only the side AB is 5 cm long
Its sides are 5 cm, 5 cm and 2.5 cm

stem: Is there a 4-sided figure with all sides 5 cm that is not a square? Take AB = AC = 5 cm with angle BAC not equal to 90°.
options: No; four equal sides always force four right angles
Yes, but only when two of its sides are made longer
No; arcs of 5 cm from B and C can never meet
Yes; 5 cm arcs from B and C give D for such a figure
explanation: Correct option: (D). With AB = AC = 5 cm and angle BAC not 90°, arcs of radius 5 cm from B and C meet at a point D (other than A), so ABDC has all four sides 5 cm but its angles are not 90°: it is not a square. Equal sides do not force right angles, no side needs to be longer, and the arcs do meet, just as in the House construction.
